boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented SJSU rituals and recurring campus celebrations, from blue-and-gold Thursdays to the ceremonial mace at graduation.

cards.title: Wear Spartan blue and gold on Thursday
cards.subtitle: Weekly SJSU pride tradition
cards.notes: Pull on blue and gold on Thursday, whether you are on campus or away, and join the university’s recurring display of Spartan pride.
cards.short_summary: A weekly invitation to visibly represent SJSU.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU identifies Spartan Pride Thursdays as a tradition of wearing Spartan blue and gold every Thursday.
cards.access_notes: Participate wherever you are; wearing blue and gold is the described activity.

cards.title: Start the Spartan welcome at Admitted Spartan Day
cards.subtitle: Spring campus welcome tradition
cards.notes: If you are admitted, use the spring visit to explore campus resources and learn the next enrollment steps directly from SJSU.
cards.short_summary: A spring welcome day for newly admitted Spartans.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU lists Admitted Spartan Day as a spring tradition where new Spartans learn campus resources and enrollment next steps.
cards.access_notes: Intended for admitted students; consult the university for the current event details.

cards.title: Join the Weeks of Welcome kickoff
cards.subtitle: Opening-weeks SJSU tradition
cards.notes: Look for Spartan-spirit events during the first weeks of the term to reconnect, meet new classmates, and ease into campus life.
cards.short_summary: An early-semester series welcoming returning and new students.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU describes Weeks of Welcome as first-weeks-of-semester events supporting returning students and new students’ transition.
cards.access_notes: Occurs during the first weeks of a semester; check SJSU event communications for specifics.

cards.title: Ask an SJSU guide for directions
cards.subtitle: Semester-start campus help tradition
cards.notes: Stop at an Ask Me table in the first days of fall or spring when you need a route to class or a quick campus answer.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU says Ask Me tables staff, faculty and administrators help answer questions and provide directions in the first days of fall and spring.
cards.access_notes: Available during the first few days of the fall and spring semesters.

cards.title: Mark Homecoming with the Spartan community
cards.subtitle: Annual SJSU Homecoming tradition
cards.notes: Follow the week’s listed events, from campus celebrations to Spartan football, and use your Tower ID when an event requires check-in.
cards.short_summary: A weeklong annual celebration connecting students, employees and alumni.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU calls Homecoming a beloved annual tradition bringing together students, faculty, staff and alumni for a week of Spartan-pride events.
cards.access_notes: Annual event; SJSU’s Homecoming page posts current programming and check-in requirements.

cards.title: Gather for Fire on the Fountain
cards.subtitle: Homecoming tradition at Tower Lawn
cards.notes: Add Fire on the Fountain to your Homecoming plan and meet at Tower Lawn for the university’s scheduled evening of Spartan spirit.
cards.short_summary: A named Homecoming rally centered on Tower Lawn.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU’s 2026 Homecoming page identifies Fire on the Fountain as its 20th annual event and calls it a Spartan-pride tradition.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled as part of Homecoming; see the university event page for the current date and attendance details.

cards.title: Explore SJSU’s Legacy Month
cards.subtitle: October equity and social-justice tradition
cards.notes: Use October programming to learn how SJSU commemorates its equity and social-justice legacy, including Smith and Carlos’ 1968 protest.
cards.short_summary: An October observance of the university’s social-justice legacy.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU states that every October it honors its equity and social-justice legacy through Legacy Month, including alumni Tommie Smith and John Carlos’ 1968 Olympic protest.
cards.access_notes: Held every October; consult SJSU programming for current events.

cards.title: Take part in Sustainability Week
cards.subtitle: SJSU Earth Day tradition
cards.notes: Watch for Earth Day and Sustainability Week activities to connect with SJSU’s stated sustainability value and its Earth Day legacy.
cards.short_summary: A campus observance tied to alumnus and Earth Day founder Gaylord Nelson.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU lists Earth Day/Sustainability Week as a tradition and notes that alumnus Gaylord Nelson founded Earth Day.
cards.access_notes: Check SJSU sustainability communications for current activities.

cards.title: Find the spring poetry celebration
cards.subtitle: SJSU literary tradition
cards.notes: Look for the spring celebration of SJSU’s poetry legacy and use it as a way into the campus literary community and programming.
cards.short_summary: A spring observance of the university’s poetic history.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU describes Legacy of Poetry as a spring celebration of a poetic legacy dating to Edwin Markham’s time at the university.
cards.access_notes: Celebrated every spring; consult SJSU programming for current events.

cards.title: Watch for the ceremonial mace at commencement
cards.subtitle: Spring and fall SJSU graduation tradition
cards.notes: At commencement, look for the SJSU ceremonial mace carried by officials and notice the artwork created to represent students’ journeys.
cards.short_summary: A distinctive SJSU commencement procession element.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU says its spring and fall commencement ceremonies include a ceremonial mace, designed by lecturer and alumna Yvonne Escalante.
cards.access_notes: Appears in SJSU spring and fall commencement ceremonies.
